title: Making the Zeros True: Fitting the Joint Offsets of a Leg From Where the Foot Was Measured, and What It Cannot Fix

artifact.note: calibrating a leg: the three joint angles are read from servos whose zero was set when the horn was pressed on, so each has an unknown offset; given the angles commanded at a number of poses and the places where the foot was then measured (on a jig or a ruled board), the offsets are found by Gauss-Newton on the difference between the foot's measured and predicted places, with the Jacobian of 34-02 (the normal equations of three unknowns, solved with a relative test for singularity), and the residual that remains is the part that offsets cannot explain (a link length that is wrong)
